columns.name: strain_name
columns.note: Matches kgBuilderClaudeSkills.py:347-348 -- rdfs:label on the SAMPLE node (taxon_uri), not the ORGANISM node.

columns.name: ncbi_taxon_id
columns.note: Matches kgBuilderClaudeSkills.py:363 -- biolink:in_taxon lives on the ORGANISM node, not the SAMPLE node. Only emitted when ncbi_taxon_id is present and has already passed live NCBI validation upstream of CSVW generation; rows lacking it fall through to the existing name-based resolver, not this mapping.

columns.name: genome_accession
columns.note: On SAMPLE, matching where kgBuilderClaudeSkills.py:368 puts the existing Accession column's dcterms:identifier.

columns.name: Project ID
columns.note: Handled by add_document_provenance() in render_submission_rdf.py instead -- that function unconditionally mints a PROJECT node per row (from this column if present, else from doc_id) and connects it, matching kgBuilderClaudeSkills.py:315-321,355 exactly. A plain CSVW column mapping can't express the 'always mint, with a fallback' behavior.

columns.name: PMC ID
columns.note: Handled by add_document_provenance() instead -- the real builder routes this through an intermediate IAO section resource (kgBuilderClaudeSkills.py:323-333,358-362), not a direct SAMPLE-to-PMC triple, which is more than a column-to-predicate mapping can express.

columns.name: biome
columns.note: Predicate fixed to match kgBuilderClaudeSkills.py:390/399 (mvikg:has_biome) -- this mapping previously used a nonexistent mvikg:biome.

columns.name: evidence
columns.note: Consumed by the review/evidence step (ECO:0000305 / ECO:0000035 pattern), not mapped directly to a triple here.

tableSchema.note: Table default subject is now the SAMPLE node (matches kgBuilderClaudeSkills.py's taxon_uri), not the ORGANISM node. The ORGANISM node and the sosa:isSampleOf / rdf:type sosa:Sample triples connecting the two are minted by add_sample_organism_structure() in render_submission_rdf.py -- this file's per-column aboutUrl overrides place each triple on the correct one of the two, but CSVW's row-at-a-time model can't mint the second node or the edge between them itself.
